# Dependency Upgrade

**Version:** `1.0.0` · **License:** [MIT](../../LICENSE)

## Purpose

Upgrade packages, frameworks, runtimes, SDKs, compilers, or build tools while
preserving supported behavior.

## When it applies

This skill applies to version bumps, security updates, dependency conflicts,
and same-technology major upgrades. Replacing the technology itself is outside
its scope.

## Capabilities

- Inventories direct, transitive, generated, and configuration dependencies.
- Selects a supported target version from authoritative upstream evidence.
- Updates manifests, lockfiles, APIs, configuration, and generated code.
- Removes obsolete compatibility paths and resolves dependency conflicts.
- Verifies behavior, security, licensing, deployment, and rollback concerns.

## Sample prompts

- "Upgrade Nuxt and remove old compatibility code."
- "Bump this project to the latest major version of React and fix breakages."
- "Update our dependencies to patch the reported security vulnerabilities."
- "Move this service to the new major version of the SDK."
- "Upgrade our build tooling and clean up any legacy config it leaves behind."

| Roo | `.roo/skills/dependency-upgrade/` or `.agents/skills/dependency-upgrade/` | `~/.roo/skills/dependency-upgrade/` or `~/.agents/skills/dependency-upgrade/` |

Paths under **Current project** are relative to the project's root
directory. Paths under **All projects** are personal locations.

On macOS, Linux, and other Unix-like systems, `~/` refers to the current user's
home directory and can be used as written. On Windows, replace a leading `~`
with `%USERPROFILE%` in Command Prompt or File Explorer, or with `$HOME` in
PowerShell. For example, `~/.agents/skills/dependency-upgrade/` becomes
`%USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills\dependency-upgrade\` or `$HOME/.agents/skills/dependency-upgrade/`.

Create one of the directories shown above, extract the ZIP contents directly
into it, and confirm that `SKILL.md` is immediately inside that directory.

When upgrading an installed skill, first empty its existing skill directory,
then extract the new ZIP into that directory. Back up any local modifications
before emptying it.
